classification.classification_note: A crafted CoolKey private EC key is misclassified as a public EC key, so `sc_pkcs15emu_object_add()` copies `sizeof(struct sc_pkcs15_pubkey_info)` bytes from the smaller stack `struct sc_pkcs15_prkey_info` object.

bug_description.original: Crash Type: stack-buffer-overflow READ in `sc_pkcs15emu_object_add`, reached from `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init` and `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init_ex` in the `honggfuzz_asan_opensc` `fuzz_pkcs15_reader` target.
bug_description.normalized: The staged fake-reader transcript makes the CoolKey PKCS#15 emulator read a 70-byte V1 object whose fixed attributes decode to `CKA_CLASS = CKO_PRIVATE_KEY` and whose explicit `CKA_KEY_TYPE` integer is `CKK_EC`. `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init()` therefore enters its private-key case, prepares `prkey_info`, and keeps `obj_info` pointing at that private-key structure. In the EC sub-branch it incorrectly assigns `obj_type = SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC` instead of `SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PRKEY_EC`. `sc_pkcs15emu_object_add()` dispatches on that public-key type, chooses `data_len = sizeof(struct sc_pkcs15_pubkey_info)` (464), allocates a 464-byte destination, and then `memcpy`s 464 bytes from the smaller `prkey_info` stack object, producing the observed stack-buffer-overflow read.

source.code:
r = coolkey_read_object(card, obj->id, 0, new_obj_data, buf_len,
                priv->nonce, sizeof(priv->nonce));
source.description: First project-side load on the crashing path that materializes the crafted CoolKey object bytes into memory for later attribute parsing.
source.value_from: The staged 294-byte `poc`, which `fuzz_add_reader()` stores as the fake smart-card transcript and `fuzz_reader_transmit()` serves back as APDU responses. Decoding the saved witness under `fuzz_get_chunk()`'s 2-byte chunk format yields a 70-byte READ_OBJECT payload beginning `01 00 00 01 00 90 00 30 b3 00 02 ... 00 00 01 00 01 00 00 00 03 ...` on the crashing path.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The copy size is 464 bytes because the object type was misclassified as a public key, but `data` still points at the smaller stack `prkey_info` object.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 464` here. In the same `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init` frame, ASan places `prkey_info` at stack offsets `[7712,8152)`, so reading 464 bytes overruns that 440-byte object by 24 bytes into the redzone before `key_type`.

root_cause.description: The EC private-key branch assigns a public-key PKCS#15 type while `obj_info` still refers to `prkey_info`, creating the later size mismatch.
root_cause.note: The fixing diff changes this assignment to `SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PRKEY_EC` and also skips unknown object classes instead of falling through.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzz input buffer is stored as the fake reader transcript; later `fuzz_get_chunk()` and `fuzz_reader_transmit()` calls slice APDU payloads from this saved `Data`/`Size` pair.

parser_admitted.description: CoolKey card detection accepted the crafted transcript and entered the object-enumeration path that the saved crash stack shows.

evidence_limitations: The saved run does not preserve APDU-by-APDU logging or the exact `SC_CARDCTL_COOLKEY_GET_NEXT_OBJECT` iteration number that supplied the crashing object; the trace is grounded to the decoded 70-byte witness READ_OBJECT payload and the single crashing `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init` loop seen in ASan.
Stage 02 did not execute a fixed-source run. `patch_resolves` is inferred from the diff's one-line type correction, not from a witnessed fixed binary.

coarse_trace.summary: A crafted 70-byte CoolKey V1 object is read from the fake-reader transcript into memory for attribute parsing.
The object metadata is interpreted as `CKO_PRIVATE_KEY` with `CKK_EC`, so the initializer prepares `prkey_info` as a private-key object.
Bug: the EC private-key case assigns `obj_type = SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC` instead of the private-key EC type.
Dispatch on the misclassified public-key type chooses a 464-byte copy size and `memcpy` overreads the 440-byte `prkey_info` stack object.

fine_trace.code:
r = coolkey_read_object(card, obj->id, 0, new_obj_data, buf_len,
                priv->nonce, sizeof(priv->nonce));
fine_trace.note: The CoolKey driver reads one crafted object body from the saved fake-card transcript into `new_obj_data`. Decoding the staged witness under `fuzz_get_chunk()`'s format yields a 70-byte V1 object payload that starts `01 00 00 01 00 90 00 30 b3 00 02 ... 00 00 01 00 01 00 00 00 03 ...`; those bytes later supply the class and key-type values on the crashing path.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned long fixed_attributes = bebytes2ulong(object_head->fixed_attributes_values);
return coolkey_get_attribute_data_fixed(attr_type, fixed_attributes, attribute);
fine_trace.note: When `CKA_CLASS` is requested for the V1 object from step 0, bytes `90 00 30 b3` are converted to `fixed_attributes = 0x900030b3`. `coolkey_get_attribute_data_fixed(CKA_CLASS, ...)` then extracts `cka_class = 3` and returns the 4-byte class value `00 00 00 03`.
The class bytes from step 1 are converted into the scalar `obj_class = 3`, i.e. `CKO_PRIVATE_KEY`. This value controls the object-class switch in `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init`.

Because step 2 produced `obj_class = CKO_PRIVATE_KEY`, execution enters the private-key case and requests `CKA_KEY_TYPE`. For the witness object from step 0, the explicit V1 integer attribute `00 00 01 00 01 00 00 00 03` supplies `key_type = 3`, i.e. `CKK_EC`, so the RSA default path is not taken.

Still in the private-key case, `obj_info` is bound to the stack `prkey_info` structure that will be passed into `sc_pkcs15emu_object_add()`. The ASan frame layout later shows this stack object occupying offsets `[7712,8152)`, so its extent is 440 bytes.

Root cause. On the private EC-key path, the code assigns the public-key PKCS#15 type `SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC` even though the data pointer remains `obj_info = &prkey_info`. The fix changes this specific enum constant to `SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PRKEY_EC`.

Class dispatch uses the misclassified `type = SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC` from step 5, so it takes the public-key case and sets `data_len` to `sizeof(struct sc_pkcs15_pubkey_info)` = 464. That 464-byte copy size matches the ASan-reported read size and already exceeds the 440-byte `prkey_info` source from step 4.

The function allocates a 464-byte destination and then copies 464 bytes from `data`, which still points at `prkey_info`. ASan reports the resulting `READ of size 464` here; since `prkey_info` ends at stack offset 8152, the copy reads 24 bytes past that object into the redzone and triggers the stack-buffer-overflow.

format.name: fuzz_pkcs15_reader fake-reader transcript
format.contract: The staged witness is a 294-byte fake-reader transcript consumed by `fuzz_get_chunk()`. On the crashing path, one READ_OBJECT response materializes a 70-byte CoolKey V1 object whose fixed attributes bytes are `90 00 30 b3` (decoding to `CKA_CLASS = CKO_PRIVATE_KEY`) and whose explicit `CKA_KEY_TYPE` integer bytes are `00 00 00 03` (`CKK_EC`). Those exact metadata values are sufficient to drive `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init()` into the buggy EC private-key branch and trigger the misclassification `SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC`; this contract does not generalize beyond that witnessed private-EC-key object.
